Choose a source-appropriate section order and primary call to action. Preserve the purpose and user-facing fields of any source contact form, but do not claim a static form submits successfully. Use relevant same-site logo and photographs where available. Write concise original copy. Avoid filler, generic repeated card grids, unsupported testimonials, invented guarantees, decorative gradients, and arbitrary industry/location stereotypes. Make mobile layout, keyboard focus, reduced motion, contrast, and semantic structure intentional.

The pipeline requests three ordered CSS parts, then four ordered HTML chunks in a fresh guest conversation in the same browser tab. The first HTML prompt receives the accepted CSS as reference context. Each response must contain exactly one fenced code block with its required first-line marker and the matching run token and part label outside the fence. Return only that part and the required token/label; do not include research notes, a source audit, rationale, or other prose. Use a CSS fence for CSS and literal source text in a `text` fence for HTML. Do not return an HTML preview or rendered artifact. Keep the assembled artifacts compatible as `index.html` and `styles.css`.

VISUAL AND UX DIRECTION:
Derive a distinctive visual system from the source site's visible identity and audience. Prioritize its actual logo, colors, photography, language, and motifs; refresh them thoughtfully rather than copying the existing layout. Use a location only when the source confirms it and it informs the audience or design.

Set an intentional palette, type pairing, spacing, image treatment, and one or two relevant motifs. Build a clear hierarchy and purposeful section composition around the organization's real conversion path. Match images to their subjects. Avoid filler sections, generic gradients, repeated card grids, and decorative complexity without a usability purpose.

Design mobile deliberately: adapt navigation, image crops, content order, spacing, and CTA prominence. Keep the result readable, keyboard usable, and accessible at all viewport sizes. Use an HTML5 UP template only as structural inspiration when a named template genuinely fits; otherwise choose an original direction.
